The *Tikaatthuddhāra* (Ds 2.4.1) is a section of the *Dhammasaṅgaṇī*, the foundational treatise of the Theravāda Abhidhamma Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. It forms part of the text's elucidatory apparatus, specifically handling the triplets (*tika*) of the Abhidhamma matrix (*mātikā*) by extracting or condensing their exposition. SuttaCentral registers one modern translation of this section in a single language [SuttaCentral].
No independent secondary literature passages discussing the *Tikaatthuddhāra* directly were identified in the reference corpus. However, text-reuse analyses by DharmaNexus demonstrate extensive structural and textual continuity within canonical and post-canonical Pali Abhidhamma literature. The text shares thousands of characters with its direct counterpart, the *Dukaatthuddhāra* (Ds 2.4.2), as well as with the preceding *Dukanikkhepa* (Ds 2.3.2) and *Tikanikkhepa* (Ds 2.3.1) [DharmaNexus]. Passages are also shared with several chapters of the *Vibhaṅga* (notably the *Khandhavibhaṅga*, *Āyatanavibhaṅga*, *Indriyavibhaṅga*, *Dhammahadayavibhaṅga*, and *Dhātuvibhaṅga*), the *Paṭṭhāna* (*Vitakkattika*), and commentarial treatises such as the *Dhammasaṅgaṇi-aṭṭhakathā*, *Abhidhammāvatāra*, and *Visuddhimagga-mahāṭīkā* [DharmaNexus].
